newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA'S CITROEN TO CUT 800 JOBS.
newsitem.headline: PSA'S CITROEN TO CUT 800 JOBS.

text.p: Automobiles Citroen, a branch of the car manufacturing group PSA Peugeot Citroen, will propose a plan that includes 800 job cuts between May 1997 and September 1998, a spokesman for Citroen said on Friday.

The cuts will be achieved mainly through early retirements, the spokesman said. The plan, scheduled to be presented to a works council on April 15, will also include 382 transfers and job conversions.
The spokesman said the plan was necessary to allow Citroen to adapt to the uncertain outlook for the European car market.
The plan will have the most impact on the Aulnay and Rennes sites and the Paris headquarters.
Citroen, which employed 40,000 people in 1984, cut 689 jobs last year after eliminating 1,180 in 1995.

PSA Peugeot Citroen is expected to report a fall in profit for 1996 later this month. Although it does not break out the Peugeot and Citroen branch results, Citroen is believed by analysts to be the weaker division.
The PSA group's domestic rival Renault SA reported a 5.25 billion franc ($932 million) loss for 1996 and plans to cut nearly 6,000 jobs in France and Belgium this year.
